“The eleventh mountain had trees full of many different kinds of fruit. The believers from that mountain are like this:

2. “They suffered for the name of the Son of God.[a] They suffered willingly, with all their hearts, and gave up their lives.”

3. “Sir,” I say, “all the trees bear fruit. Why are some of their fruits more beautiful?[b]” He says, “Listen. God honors everyone who has suffered for the name. All their sins have been taken away because they suffered for the name of the Son of God. Now hear why their fruits differ and some are better than others.”

4. “Some were brought before the authorities and questioned. They did not deny but suffered willingly. The Lord honors them even more. Their fruit is the best. Others became afraid and hesitated. They wondered whether to deny or confess, but they still suffered. Their fruits are smaller because that thought arose in their hearts. It is an evil thought for a servant to deny their own master.”

5. “If you are thinking this way, take care. Do not let the thought stay in your hearts, or you may die to God. You who suffer for the name should glorify God. God considered you worthy to bear this name and to have all your sins healed.”

6. “So count yourselves blessed.[c] Yet when one of you suffers for God, you think you have done something great. The Lord gives you life, but you do not understand. Your sins weighed you down. If you had not suffered for the name of the Lord,[d] you would have died to God because of your sins.”

7. “I say this to you who hesitate between denial and confession. Confess that you have a Lord. If you deny him, you may be handed over to prison.”

8. “The nations punish their servants if they deny their own master. What, then, do you think the Lord will do to you? He has authority over all. Remove these thoughts from your hearts so that you may live to God forever.”

translation:
  text: '“The believers from the eleventh mountain, where trees were full of fruit and adorned with many
    different kinds of fruit, are like this:


    2. “They are those who suffered for the name of the Son of God,[a] who suffered willingly with all
    their hearts and gave up their lives.”


    3. “Why, then, sir,” I say, “do all the trees bear fruit, but some of their fruits are more beautiful?[b]”
    “Listen,” he says. “All who have ever suffered for the name are honored before God, and all their
    sins have been taken away, because they suffered for the name of the Son of God. Now hear why their
    fruits differ and some surpass the others.”


    4. “Those who were brought before the authorities and examined, and did not deny but suffered willingly,
    are even more honored before the Lord. Theirs is the surpassing fruit. But those who became fearful
    and hesitant, and considered in their hearts whether they would deny or confess, yet suffered—their
    fruits are smaller, because this thought arose in their hearts. For it is an evil thought that a servant
    should deny their own master.”


    5. “So take care, you who consider these things, lest this thought remain in your hearts and you die
    to God. You who suffer for the name ought to glorify God, because God considered you worthy to bear
    this name and to have all your sins healed.”


    6. “So count yourselves blessed.[c] Yet you think you have done a great deed if one of you suffers
    for God. The Lord grants you life, and you do not understand. Your sins weighed you down; if you had
    not suffered for the name of the Lord,[d] you would have died to God because of your sins.”


    7. “I say these things to you who hesitate between denial and confession. Confess that you have a
    Lord, lest by denying him you be handed over to prison.”


    8. “If the nations punish their servants when one denies their own master, what do you think the Lord
    will do to you, he who has authority over all? Remove these thoughts from your hearts, so that you
    may live to God forever.”'

  yaml_path: translation/extra_canonical/shepherd_of_hermas/105.yaml
  text: '“The believers from the eleventh mountain, where trees were full of fruit and adorned with many
    different kinds of fruit, are like this:


    2. “They are those who suffered for the name of the Son of God,[a] who suffered willingly with all
    their hearts and gave up their lives.”


    3. “Why, then, sir,” I say, “do all the trees bear fruit, but some of their fruits are more beautiful?[b]”
    “Listen,” he says. “All who have ever suffered for the name are honored before God, and all their
    sins have been taken away, because they suffered for the name of the Son of God. Now hear why their
    fruits differ and some surpass the others.”


    4. “Those who were brought before the authorities and examined, and did not deny but suffered willingly,
    are even more honored before the Lord. Theirs is the surpassing fruit. But those who became fearful
    and hesitant, and considered in their hearts whether they would deny or confess, yet suffered—their
    fruits are smaller, because this thought arose in their hearts. For it is an evil thought that a servant
    should deny their own master.”


    5. “So take care, you who consider these things, lest this thought remain in your hearts and you die
    to God. You who suffer for the name ought to glorify God, because God considered you worthy to bear
    this name and to have all your sins healed.”


    6. “So count yourselves blessed.[c] Yet you think you have done a great deed if one of you suffers
    for God. The Lord grants you life, and you do not understand. Your sins weighed you down; if you had
    not suffered for the name of the Lord,[d] you would have died to God because of your sins.”


    7. “I say these things to you who hesitate between denial and confession. Confess that you have a
    Lord, lest by denying him you be handed over to prison.”


    8. “If the nations punish their servants when one denies their own master, what do you think the Lord
    will do to you, he who has authority over all? Remove these thoughts from your hearts, so that you
    may live to God forever.”'
